description:
FOUND s437 (Fable review of s434-s436) by a phase-model probe; PRE-EXISTING
(identical on the 4356e77 base worktree) -- not the phase model's doing.

REPRODUCERS (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL HEAD):
  our $t = "m"; package A; $t .= "A"; package main; print "$t\n";
      perl: mA      PCL: m
  our @o = (1); package A; print scalar(@o), "\n"; package main; print scalar(@o), "\n";
      perl: 1 1     PCL: 0 1
  { our @o; package A; push @o, "x"; package main; print scalar(@o), "|@o|\n"; }
      perl: 1|x|    PCL: 1|x|   (the in-BLOCK spelling is requalified -- #239 + #251/M7)

WHY: `our NAME` binds the bare name to the DECLARING package's variable for
the rest of the enclosing LEXICAL scope, and a later `package` statement does
not re-home it.  `_requalify_block_our_after_pkg_switch` (Parser2.pm) does
that rewrite for a region INSIDE A BLOCK; at FILE level the `package A;`
statement opens a new emission SECTION and the unqualified `$t` in that
section is emitted as A's `$t`.  So a file-level `our` followed by a top-level
`package` switch reads/writes the wrong variable -- silently.

HOW COMMON: rare in the in-repo populations (not measured); the common idiom
declares `our` INSIDE the package it belongs to.  Test files that declare
`our @warnings` / `our $x` in main and then `package Foo;` to build a helper
are the shape to look for.

FIX SHAPE (not designed): the same requalification the block pass does, run
over the file's top-level section boundaries -- the declaring section's `our`
names carry into later sections until a same-name redeclaration (the #251/M7
truncation rule).  It is a SCOPING change: the sweep IS the gate (WHAT-TO-RUN
table), plus a gate-SET scan over both populations, plus the probes above as
both_agree guard rows.  Filler-sized.

(Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08, resumed s536; commit "s535a D2: the package-region residues on the binder".)  A FILE-level `our $t` alias read in a LATER top-level section of another package (`our $t = "m"; package A; $t .= "A"`) is now spelled in the declaring package: `_requalify_spanning_ours` asks Pl::Binder::spans with kinds => our (the same span question port 3 asks for my/state) and rewrites exactly the alias's uses (`_refers_to_decl` skip) through the requalifier's `_rewrite_var_uses` -- a section boundary instead of a block one.  Probe d475: perl `mA | 1 | 1 | 1|x|`, base `m | 0 | ...`, tree = perl.  Guards Pl/t/span-binder-01.t row 15 (FAILS on 06a4b8ba) + row 16 (control: a plain `our` statement in a sub region, passes on both).  Status left as it is.
